prompt.context: PCC is one of the cricket franchises in the world's largest cricket league, LPI. Despite having one of the strongest teams in the league, PCC has continuously disappointed its fans and owners and has failed to live up to its true potential. Mr. Gandhi has recently replaced Mr. Modi as the new CEO of PCC. Mr. Gandhi has been handed the task of turning around the fortunes of PCC. He has been an ardent cricket fan and player of the sport all his life and also has a track record of turning around corporates. Mr. Gandhi has hired you to investigate and recommend on the action plan.
prompt.question: How would you investigate and recommend an action plan to improve PCC's profitability and turn around the franchise?

clarifying_info.q: How do we define success for this engagement?
clarifying_info.a: Success is defined based on improved profitability.

clarifying_info.q: Has there been any significant change in the team roster recently?
clarifying_info.a: The team has been relatively stable with no abnormal changes.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a budget available for player acquisitions?
clarifying_info.a: The owners are willing to incur Capex to attract up to two star-performers in the auction.

clarifying_info.q: How is PCC's brand perceived in the market?
clarifying_info.a: PCC lacks brand recall and is amongst the lowest in the league.

clarifying_info.q: Are other franchises in the league profitable?
clarifying_info.a: All franchisees in the league are profit making.

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall market trend for cricket?
clarifying_info.a: The overall cricket viewership and popularity has been on the rise (assume pre-covid time).

exhibits.title: LPI Team Rankings for the Last 3 Years and Average Star Rating Score
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing league rankings for 8 teams (CSC, DDC, HYC, KKC, MMC, PCC, RBC, RJC) across three years (2018, 2019, 2020), where a higher bar indicates better performance. A second chart shows each team's Average Star-Rating Score on a 0 to 7 scale.
exhibits.data: Teams: CSC, DDC, HYC, KKC, MMC, PCC, RBC, RJC. Star rating scale 0.0 to 7.0. PCC bars are consistently at or near the bottom of league rankings across all three years. PCC average star rating is among the lowest of all teams.

exhibits.title: Star Players Available for Auction
exhibits.shows: Two tables listing star batsmen and star bowlers available for auction, each showing signing fee (USD Mn), games played, runs scored (batsmen) or wickets taken (bowlers), and star rating out of 10. Average-per-game columns are not shown to the candidate.
exhibits.data: Star batsmen: VK (15.0 USD Mn, 200 games, 6000 runs, Star 10), MD (15.0, 200, 4800, Star 9), RS (12.0, 200, 6000, Star 8), DW (10.5, 150, 5250, Star 7), CG (12.0, 130, 5200, Star 9). Star bowlers: LM (7.0, 125, 200 wickets, Star 7), YC (5.5, 100, 121, Star 6), JB (8.0, 75, 140, Star 9), AM (5.5, 150, 175, Star 6), DS (10.0, 70, 97, Star 8). Maximum permitted budget for acquisitions is $20mn.

exhibits.title: PCC Predicted Yearly League Ranking (3 Years) and LPI Prize Money Distribution
exhibits.shows: A grouped bar chart comparing PCC predicted rank distribution with and without acquisitions across four rank tiers (Below-5, Top-5, Top-3, Top-2), and a prize money table by rank tier.
exhibits.data: With acquisitions: Below-5=0%, Top-5=65%, Top-3=30%, Top-2=5%. Without acquisitions: Below-5=55%, Top-5=35%, Top-3=10%, Top-2=0%. Prize money: Below-5=$0Mn, Top-5=$10Mn, Top-3=$20Mn, Top-2=$50Mn.

framework: Improve Profit = Increase Revenue + Reduce Costs

Increase Revenue — two levers: (a) improve existing revenue streams: increase ticket sales, increase non-ticket income (broadcasting rights, sponsorship, merchandise); (b) add new revenue streams: ancillary businesses

Reduce Costs — two levers: (a) reduce player fee through success-linked fee structures and trading or releasing non-performing expensive players; (b) reduce staff, corporate, and other operational expenses

Key strategic insight: Given PCC's low brand recall and consistent underperformance, focus must be on revenue improvement. Team performance and brand value are tightly linked, pointing to acquiring star players as the primary lever

Business model context (interviewer background only): Key revenue streams = Broadcasting Rights, Sponsorship, Ticket Sales, Merchandise Sale, Player Trading. Major cost heads = Player Fee (30-35%), Franchise Fee (20%)

questions.prompt: Looking at Exhibit 1, what observations can you make about PCC's performance and what might be driving it?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that PCC has consistently underperformed across all three years. A strong candidate calculates or estimates average ranking across 2018-2019-2020 to confirm PCC is last or near-last on average. Candidate should connect low team performance to low star rating and hypothesize that acquiring star players would improve both the star rating and on-field results, thereby improving brand value and all revenue streams.

math.setup: Compare each team's ranking across 3 years; calculate PCC average ranking vs. others. Compare PCC star rating vs. league average.
steps: PCC bars in 2018, 2019, 2020 are consistently among the shortest, indicating last or near-last finish each year.
PCC average star rating reads approximately 1-2 on the 0-7 scale vs. top teams (CSC, DDC) near 6-7.
Conclusion: PCC has a systemic squad quality problem, not a one-year anomaly.
math.answer: PCC ranks consistently last or near-last over 3 years and has the lowest average star rating in the league, indicating a structural quality gap in the squad that drives both poor results and low brand value.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, which two players would you recommend PCC acquire within the $20mn budget cap, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should derive a performance efficiency metric to compare players objectively rather than relying on raw totals. Ideal metric: average runs per game (batsmen) and average wickets per match (bowlers). Candidate then ranks by efficiency, applies the budget constraint ($20mn total), and considers star rating for brand impact. Ideal answer: CG (batsman) + JB (bowler). Interviewer may prompt candidate to calculate averages if they do not do so proactively.

math.setup: Avg. Score/Game = Runs Scored / Games Played for batsmen. Avg. Wickets/Match = Wickets Taken / Games Played for bowlers. Then find the best-performing pair within the $20mn budget.
steps: Batsmen averages: VK=6000/200=30, MD=4800/200=24, RS=6000/200=30, DW=5250/150=35, CG=5200/130=40. Highest average: CG at 40 runs/game.
Bowler averages: LM=200/125=1.60, YC=121/100=1.21, JB=140/75=1.87, AM=175/150=1.17, DS=97/70=1.39. Highest average: JB at 1.87 wickets/match.
Budget check: CG ($12mn) + JB ($8mn) = $20mn, exactly within budget.
Star rating: CG (9) + JB (9) = combined 18, highest combined star rating of any within-budget pair.
math.answer: Acquire CG (batsman, $12mn, 40 runs/game avg, Star 9) and JB (bowler, $8mn, 1.87 wickets/match avg, Star 9). They have the highest per-game performance metrics, fit exactly within $20mn, and deliver the highest combined star rating.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, quantify the financial impact of the acquisition. Is the $20mn investment justified?
questions.guidance: Candidate calculates probability-weighted expected prize money for both scenarios, computes incremental annual profit, and assesses payback period. A strong candidate proactively asks for data to quantify impact before the exhibit is shared. A great candidate also notes that prize money understates the total upside because improved star rating drives higher sponsorship, ticket premiums, and merchandise revenues on top.

math.setup: Expected annual prize money = sum of (probability x prize) for each rank tier. Compare with-acquisition vs. without-acquisition.
steps: Payback on $20mn investment from prize money alone: ~2 years
Additional upside not captured: higher brand value drives more sponsorship revenue, premium ticket pricing, and merchandise sales
math.answer: Acquisition generates approximately $10mn additional prize money per year over 3 years. The $20mn upfront cost is recovered within 2 years from prize money alone. Total return is materially higher when non-prize revenue uplift from improved brand value is included.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some additional revenue streams that PCC can look to add to their operations in order to support the company turnaround and profitability?

categories.name: Fan Engagement and Membership
ideas: Create a paid fan club with special privileges such as priority ticket access, lunch with players, and behind-the-scenes content
Ultra-Premium Membership offering seats close to players, hotel and lounge access for away games, and similar exclusive incentives

categories.name: Digital and Media
ideas: Launch a mobile gaming app (fantasy cricket, simulation games) featuring PCC players
Launch a sports magazine, sports website, or online talk show to generate advertising revenue

categories.name: Brand and Merchandise
ideas: Expand merchandising revenue through online and physical retail
Co-branded credit and debit cards for fans, earning commission income on transactions

categories.name: Venue and Hospitality
ideas: Partner with co-branded cafes and sports bars near the stadium
Host non-match events at the stadium such as concerts and corporate events to monetize venue capacity

categories.name: Player Development
ideas: Start a junior cricket training academy to generate tuition revenue and build a long-term talent pipeline

recommendation: Acquire CG (batsman, $12mn, 40 avg runs/game, Star 9) and JB (bowler, $8mn, 1.87 avg wickets/match, Star 9) at the next auction — highest performance efficiency in their respective categories, exactly within the $20mn budget, and highest combined star rating
The probability-weighted prize money increases by approximately $10mn per year over 3 years, recovering the $20mn investment within 2 years even before accounting for non-prize revenue uplift
Improved star rating and better league performance will elevate PCC brand recall — currently the lowest in the league — driving upside across sponsorship fees, ticket premiums, and merchandise sales
Simultaneously pursue new revenue streams including paid fan club memberships, a mobile gaming app, and a junior training academy to diversify income and reduce dependence on prize money
risks: Star players carry high injury risk, which could reduce actual winning probability below the model projections
Team dynamics and chemistry cannot be guaranteed — new players may underperform within the franchise environment
The $20mn capital expenditure is committed upfront regardless of on-field results
next_steps: Finalize acquisition of CG and JB at the upcoming auction, ensuring total contracts stay within the $20mn cap
Develop a brand-building and fan-engagement program to convert improved on-field performance into measurable revenue uplifts
Evaluate and pilot 2-3 new revenue streams in the first season post-acquisition (paid fan club, mobile app, junior academy)
Track actual prize money, sponsorship rates, and ticket revenue year-on-year against projections and adjust strategy accordingly
